fact_text: The guest said passing oil costs to consumers was the right step, because state absorption would widen the fiscal deficit and make it harder to keep the IMF programme on track.

fact_text: The guest argued a price signal cuts demand, so passing costs through works better than holding prices, which keeps consumption high; he called work-from-home and online classes sensible conservation steps.

fact_text: The guest said that when the PTI government held fuel prices for political gain during the Russia-Ukraine oil shock, the fiscal deficit and then the current account deficit widened, pushing Pakistan into a crisis that led to an IMF programme.

fact_text: The guest said oil above $100 lasted about 7 months in 2008, about 4 months in the Arab Spring and about 4 months in the Russia-Ukraine episode, and prices partly reversed during the Russia-Ukraine episode.

fact_text: The guest said in 2008 Pakistan was in crisis with high starting valuations so the market fell, whereas in 2011-2014 low valuations let the market rally despite high oil, so oil is not the only driver.

fact_text: The guest said that at valuations near 9 times trailing earnings, as in January 2026, the odds of a good 3-year return are less clear than at 6 to 7 times earnings.

fact_text: The guest noted the market fell to about 4.75 times trailing earnings during COVID, and said low multiples do not rule out further falls if earnings deteriorate.
